system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

The remaining octets of the CBS-Message-Information-Page n contain only padding information and are not included in this parameter. In the case where the user information is encoded using the GSM 7 bit default alphabet and the last character terminates at an octet boundary, this parameter indicates the number of octets of user information. In the case where the last character does not terminate at an octet boundary, this parameter indicates the number of octets up to the octet boundary immediately following the last GSM 7 bit default alphabet character of user information. data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present, and the stated encodings and page counts match the cell broadcast page sizes. However, both texts break the UAE one-page handset advice. English is 221 GSM-7 characters across 3 pages, and Arabic is 799 UCS-2 characters across 20 pages, with the same advice paragraph repeated three times. The English text has no protective action at all, so its first page carries the hazard but no action. The drafter can fix all of these.

objections.issue: The English text is 221 GSM-7 characters, which takes 3 cell broadcast pages (93 characters per page). The UAE handset advice limits the message to 1 page.
objections.fix: Shorten the English message to 93 GSM-7 characters or fewer so it fits one page. Keep the hazard, the protective action and the end time, and drop secondary detail such as the full source line.

evidence.quote: message should be limited to 1 page
The Message Information Page then consists of 93 user characters

objections.issue: The Arabic text is 799 UCS-2 characters, which takes 20 pages. That is far beyond the 1-page limit, since an 82-octet page holds about 41 UCS-2 characters. Most of the length comes from the same advice paragraph pasted three times.
objections.fix: Remove the two duplicate copies of the advice paragraph. Then condense the Arabic message to the hazard plus one or two key actions, aiming for one page (about 41 UCS-2 characters) or as close as possible. If one page cannot be reached, flag the overrun to the people who approve the alert.
